The image shows the signature of this: at a $10^{-9}$ contact threshold only 22 of 168 points have any contact and 146 are "rattlers", yet over 1000 pairs lie within $\sim7\times10^{-9}$ of the maximum, i.e. a broad unresolved near-contact plateau rather than an exactly tied active set. A genuinely isolated minimax optimum here has $168\cdot7-28=1148$ effective degrees of freedom, so it should be near-isostatic, with on the order of 1148 active contacts (average degree $\approx13.7$), a rigid contact graph, and a nonnegative equilibrium stress balancing the tangent forces. The current best is missing exactly that rigid, stress-balanced contact structure, so LP/Adam steps can keep flattening the plateau infinitesimally without ever changing contact topology or reaching a new basin.
